name: What hidden problems could increase the cost of my kitchen renovation?

mainEntity.name: What hidden problems could increase the cost of my kitchen renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep a practical allowance for concealed conditions, but do not accept a vague “allowance” without asking what it covers and how changes are approved. Older kitchens can reveal damaged framing, outdated wiring, leaks, uneven floors, or unrecorded alterations after demolition. Context: The risk rises when walls, plumbing, electrical systems, or flooring are opened. A coordinated design and construction plan can identify likely dependencies, but no pre-demolition review can reveal everything. Key factors: - Age and prior remodeling history. - Signs of leaks, stains, pests, or uneven surfaces. - Whether utilities are being relocated. Practical guidance: Ask for a written change-order process, unit rates where possible, photo documentation, and an explanation of any allowance. Avoid approving extra work verbally without understanding price and schedule effects. Soft positioning: Elite Remodeling & Design can connect demolition findings to the design and construction decisions that follow.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common surprises include leaks, damaged framing, uneven floors, outdated wiring, poor ventilation, pests, and unrecorded prior work. Ask how concealed conditions are documented, priced, and approved, and keep a contingency. A written change-order process helps prevent confusion when demolition reveals problems.
